SPARK & the Web4 Sovereignty Loop

Four organs — Vault, Engine, Aether, Havix — form one closed loop, and SPARK is the fuel that makes it turn. The E2EE protocol stack is open for audit; this document describes the architecture as built, the token economics as designed, and the dual-track launch: a whitelisted presale followed by a public LBP-based IDO.

Abstract. Web3 gave users wallets but kept their social lives on servers. The Web4 prototype loop closes that gap with physical isolation: an online social app (Engine) that holds no keys, an offline safe (Vault) that holds keys and never connects, an SBT-governed parliament (Aether) that banks the fuel reserve, and a parallel-identity network (Havix) — master-DID derived, running a credit-and-value dual economy — that charters AI under a living constitution. $SPARK is the single issued asset that meters expression in the app, endows the DAO reserve, and flows between them — fuel for the loop, never a vote. This whitepaper documents the architecture as it exists in the public repositories, then specifies the token: utility, allocation (10% presale / 20% IDO / 10% DEX liquidity / 50% DAO reserve / 10% community incentives), the two-phase launch, the unlock schedule, and the safeguards that keep the launch fair and the reserve sovereign.

01 The Sovereignty Loop

This is one project, not a portfolio of products. Each repository is an organ; the organs share one bloodstream — SPARK. A user chats in Engine; every message burns fuel; fuel is banked in the Aether reserve; the reserve is kept liquid by chartered AI on Havix; Havix's network effects keep Engine alive; and Engine's demand gives SPARK its physical backing. Cut any organ and the loop stops turning.

02 Architecture: Isolation & Identity

2.1 Physical isolation as a security model

The loop's root security decision is separation by physics, not by policy. Engine runs online but holds zero private keys; Vault holds the keys and is built with no network permission at all — its Android manifest declares no INTERNET permission, making exfiltration a physical rather than logical problem[3]. Signing requests travel from Engine to Vault over signature-protected IPC; key material travels between devices only as encrypted QR frames — camera-to-camera, air-gap enforced[3].

The trust is auditable: Engine's core/ modules (protocol, crypto, IPC) are byte-identical to Vault's, so both apps verify against the same public source[1]. Messages are end-to-end encrypted with ECDH key agreement and AES-256-GCM; the relay sees envelopes, never plaintext[1].

2.2 One identity, four unlinkable contexts

Havix derives four context-specific sub-identities from a single master key using HKDF — public, market, tunnel and wiki contexts[6]. The derivation is cryptographically unlinkable: your market persona cannot be correlated with your private correspondence. This is what lets one person be simultaneously a citizen in the Parliament, a trader in the market, and a private person in chat — without three accounts and without a platform holding the mapping.

2.3 Three planes, one loop

  • Application plane (online): Engine — user-facing, keyless, pure-memory. Messages exist in RAM; the attack surface for seizure is roughly zero.
  • Custody plane (offline): Vault — keystores sealed behind biometrics, export only via QR.
  • Coordination plane (off-chain P2P): Havix — identity derivation, reputation/credit ledgers, arbitration, and the charter that licenses AI[6].
  • Settlement plane (on-chain): Aether on BNB Smart Chain — governance, treasury and timelocked execution, governed by soulbound SBT rank rather than transferable token supply[4][5].

Havix's own roadmap formalizes this as a three-layer stack — network bedrock (L0), cognitive execution (L1, Germ), on-chain governance (L2, Aether) — with the 4-context DID enforcing the cryptographic separation between layers[7].

03 The Four Organs

3.1 Vault — the Safe v3.60.0 · shipped

A generic offline keystore, not an Engine accessory: it can custody keys for any compliant app. Mechanism: no network permission; keystores sealed in the TEE; biometric-gated signing (StrongBox-backed where available); SPARK wallet custody — the balance lives as an append-only chain of transactions co-signed inside the secure world, and a wallet handover migrates the full balance to a new device as a genesis transaction; QR-only migration to new hardware, with the private key never entering a network stack[3]. Since v3.40 Engine reaches Vault over a signature-protected Binder IPC direct channel — the legacy cross-app jump dialogs are gone[3].

3.2 Engine — the App v3.45.1 · shipped

The market entry point of the whole loop: a sovereign social messenger with pure-memory architecture, group messaging, a 60-emoji expression economy and DID profiles[1]. Its economic engine is already specified in the repository: one kilobyte costs ten SPARK — every message is metered by its UTF-8 size, rounded up, with a floor of ten SPARK per message; a daily fuel subsidy of 1,000 SPARK (idempotent per calendar day, ruled by the authoritative ledger, gated by a bound Vault identity); heavy users top up from a wallet[2]. The wallet balance is not a stored number: it is the derivation of an append-only chain of transactions co-signed by the Vault-held wallet key — every change of balance, without exception, is a signed transaction[2]. Client-side pre-deduction is implemented; a standalone spark-ledger service settles balances server-side[2].

3.3 Aether — the Parliament v3.6 · BSC · audit closed · mainnet pending

An SBT-governed DAO kernel on BNB Smart Chain. Weight is earned, not bought: AetherRing mints 14 non-transferable soulbound ranks; three chambers (Council, Parliament, Elders) plus a citizen referendum check one another through a 7-stage proposal lifecycle with an elder veto; the treasury is a 3/5 Safe multisig executing timelocked calls[4][5]. The deliberate design tension: governance is soulbound (SBT) while the fuel is a real, issued asset — whales can buy $SPARK, but $SPARK buys messages, not votes. One contract stands apart: AetherDonation is an external philanthropy channel (USDC tips for public goods) and is independent of the loop's economics.

3.4 Havix — the Identity Root validated · standby

The coordination network beneath the loop: eight modules (identity, message-types, credit, vouch, wiki, arbitration, market, s-node runtime), 1,174 passing tests (MVP 980 + validation experiment 194, M10 audit baseline), and a two-round audit program — M9 closed all 15 findings, while the M10 deep audit surfaced 52 more (5 P0 + 15 P1 + 32 P2) with P0/P1 remediated before closed beta[6]. Its charter plane is what puts AI on a legal footing rather than a magical one: routine operations execute automatically with receipts; red-line operations are physically routed to a human, on-chain vote. The charter store and interceptor are scheduled as the M11 workstream[7].

3.5 Germ — the Brain, later

Germ is the node-level AI layer: AI that reasons with its own 4-context identities on the Havix network. It is intentionally deferred — Engine is today's market entry; the Brain arrives when the loop has users worth caring for. In this whitepaper Germ appears only where the economics must reserve room for it (reserve AI, §5).

04 SPARK Token Economics

4.1 Utility: fuel with physics behind it

SPARK is a metering asset. In Engine, every kilobyte costs 10 SPARK — metered by message size, rounded up, minimum 10 per message — the meter is in the protocol, not the terms of service[2]. Budgets derive from a real 100 Mbps relay baseline: text envelopes up to 40 KB, media up to 48 KB, a 128 KB hard frame ceiling, groups capped at 200[1]. Because every expressive byte costs fuel, spam has a marginal cost and speech stays free.

  • Acquire: daily fuel subsidy (1,000 SPARK per calendar day, idempotent, gated by a bound Vault identity[2]), wallet top-up[2], or market purchase after TGE.
  • Spend: messaging fuel; group and media budgets; SDK app usage.
  • Hold: the DAO treasury holds SPARK as its long-term reserve — demand from real usage accrues to every holder symmetrically.

◇ Design parameters (vesting lengths, LP lock, fee routing, allowance decay) are recommended defaults of this draft; each is confirmed or amended by governance before the presale opens. On-chain metering rates (1 KB = 10 SPARK, minimum 10 per message; 1,000 daily fuel subsidy per calendar day) are fixed in the Engine specification[2].

4.2 Two phases of the same asset — metering ledger, then fixed supply

SPARK ships in two deliberate stages, and the sequence is the design. Phase A — metering ledger (live today): inside shipped Engine software, SPARK exists as an off-chain hash-chained ledger. Each device mints 1,000 per calendar day through a Vault-countersigned fuel subsidy — anti-sybil defenses are already in production: a TEE/DRM device anchor, relay-side daily deduplication of unlinkable device hashes, and an amount whitelist enforced at the signing gate. Phase A balances are not transferable, not tradable, not convertible — today they are quota, not securities.

Phase B — TGE mapping (planned): the fixed 1,000T supply takes effect at TGE. Initial supply combines the presale, IDO, liquidity and reserve tranches of §4.3 with a snapshot-based mapping of Phase A balances into the community-incentive tranche — specific conversion parameters are draft defaults ◇ confirmed by governance before the presale opens. After TGE, SPARK circulates freely, including open USDC and other stablecoin pairs. The conversion channel is deliberately unbuilt today: device anchoring, daily dedup and amount whitelisting must exist before there is a vault to defend, so that the day convertibility opens, these defenses graduate from quota hygiene to vault gates.

4.3 Supply & allocation

Total supply is fixed at 1,000T SPARK (1,000,000,000,000,000 — one thousand trillion). Allocation follows the 10 / 20 / 10 / 50 / 10 split: presale, IDO, DEX liquidity, DAO reserve, community incentives. There is no team tranche, no insider allocation, no marketing tranche — the team's upside is the 50% reserve it shares with the DAO, unlocked only through public governance and capped by charter at ≤5% of the reserve per year.

04b The Dual-Track Launch

The core of the launch is presale + IDO in parallel, at different tempos: the presale targets the core community; the IDO faces the public. The presale builds the base; the IDO opens the market.

10%presale — whitelist · $500 cap
20%IDO — LBP · 3–7 days
10%liquidity — seeded at TGE
10%community incentives — referral & activation
50%DAO reserve — governance-gated · ≤5%/yr

4.4 Phase 1 — Presale (10%)

  • Audience: early core contributors and active community members only. Wallet addresses are collected into a whitelist in advance; start time is announced to the list first.
  • Anti-whale: a hard $500 per-wallet cap.
  • Terms: pay with USDT or BNB at a fixed low price; 25% unlocks at TGE, the remainder vests linearly over 9 months ◇.
  • Execution: when the window opens, whitelisted wallets connect on the official site and subscribe inside the cap.

4.5 Phase 2 — IDO (20%)

  • Platform: an LBP launchpad of the Fjord Foundry class — the price starts high and decays until demand catches it, which removes the sniping edge; no whitelist, no first-block advantage.
  • Parameters: token address triple-checked before funding the pool (irreversible); payment in USDT or BNB; a 3–7 day window; per-wallet minimum and maximum caps; starting price above the presale price.
  • Distribution: 25% of each wallet's allocation is claimable at TGE, the remainder vests linearly over 9 months ◇; proceeds flow directly to the project multisig.
  • Accounting: after the window closes, the subscription list and amounts are reconciled and published before distribution.

4.6 Liquidity & DEX (10%)

At TGE the liquidity tranche seeds the DEX pool, paired against BNB. SPARK is recommended to be issued as a BEP-20 token on BNB Chain ◇ — matching the USDT/BNB payment rails of both rounds — with the Aether treasury and governance deployed on the same BNB Smart Chain[4], so reserve operations settle natively with no cross-chain bridge[5].

Addresses are published on the Spark page at the moment of deployment. Before that moment, any address claiming to be SPARK is fraudulent.

4.7 Unlock schedule

The structural promise is a hard float ceiling: the calendar can never unlock more than 40% (presale + IDO + LP); the 10% incentive tranche pays out only against verified referrals and activations; and the 50% reserve moves only through a public, vetoable proposal, with the charter capping releases at ≤5% of the reserve per year. Early buyers know exactly what the maximum float is.

4.8 Safeguards & compliance

  • Security: token, presale and LBP contracts must carry audits from a recognized firm before any funds are accepted; reports are published alongside the addresses.
  • Transparency: presale and IDO contract addresses and rules are announced before each window opens; the subscription reconciliation is published before TGE distribution.
  • Anti-bot: LBP price decay defeats sniping; per-wallet caps ($500 presale; min/max IDO) cap concentration; dynamic slippage bounds may be applied on the presale contract ◇.
  • Legal: the launch is being reviewed by counsel for the jurisdictions involved; participation may be restricted where required. Nothing here is an offer of securities.

05 Governance of the Reserve

The 50% reserve is not a treasury wallet — it is a constitutional object. Custody sits in a 3/5 Safe multisig; every movement requires a proposal through Aether's 7-stage lifecycle, survives the elder veto window, and executes through the timelock[4][5]. Weight in that process is soulbound and earned — 14 AetherRing ranks that cannot be bought or transferred[4].

Reserve uses are bounded by charter: user-subsidy epochs for Engine fuel, relay and infrastructure funding, ecosystem grants, and — once Germ exists — liquidity management by chartered AI inside hard limits, with red lines routing back to human votes[6][7]. The charter also fixes a release-rate ceiling of ≤5% of the reserve per year — a computable promise, not a discretionary one: even a fully captured treasury cannot drain the reserve faster than one-twentieth per year. The balance design is deliberate: chambers and citizens each hold roughly half the voting weight, so neither the institution nor the crowd can spend the reserve alone[5].

07 Risks & Disclaimers

  • Execution risk: Aether mainnet deployment, the M11 charter store, and the spark-ledger service are unfinished components the TGE sequence depends on[2][7].
  • Cross-chain risk: mitigated by design — SPARK and the Aether governance/treasury deploy on the same BNB Smart Chain ◇, so reserve operations settle natively without any bridge dependency.
  • Market risk: an LBP discovers price honestly — which means it can discover it downward. Fixed low presale pricing compensates early trust but does not guarantee returns.
  • Regulatory risk: token launches face divergent regulation; restrictions may apply by jurisdiction; counsel review is a precondition, not a formality.
  • Smart-contract risk: audits reduce but never eliminate risk; only interact with addresses published on the official site.
